title: War Machine
content:
War Machine (2026) operates on a paradoxical fulcrum, initially lulling the viewer into a protracted, almost domestic slice-of-life cadence within a grueling military crucible—channeling an unyielding, pre-drifter Reacher kineticism through Alan Ritchson’s monolithic presence. Yet, this methodical psychological verisimilitude is abruptly atomized when the narrative undergoes a jarring, schizophrenic rupture, violently colliding with an asphyxiating sci-fi meat-grinder. The subsequent choreography careens between hyper-visceral, concussive close-quarters brutality and erratic, CGI-heavy bedlam that muddies the spatial geography of the set-pieces. By systematically excising nearly the entire roster of characters through an unrelenting, nihilistic attrition, the film retroactively defangs its own meticulous buildup, reducing its intricate interpersonal symbiosis to a hollow, Sisyphean exercise in narrative futility.
Rating 6.5/10
![](images/mt2i0anx.jpg)

title: Blue Eye Samurai
content:
Blue Eye Samurai is a masterclass in adult animation that elevates a simple revenge story into a morally gray, cinematic epic. Driven by stunning, fluid fight choreography, gorgeous visual art reminiscent of woodblock prints, and breathtaking, multi-layered storytelling—particularly in standout episodes like 5 and 6—the series excels by refusing to rely on easy heroes or villains. Mizu’s headlong, obsessive crusade, Akemi’s complex turn toward political power, and Taigen’s surprisingly grounded heart create a deeply tragic, compelling cast of characters. Delivering an explosive climax that seamlessly closes its first act while setting up a massive international scope, Season 1 stands as a brilliant, unforgettable triumph.
Review 8/10.
![](images/mt122i0l.jpg)

title: The Lego Batman Movie
content:
The Lego Batman Movie is a surprisingly clever satire that manages to be both a laugh-out-loud comedy and a genuinely solid character study of Bruce Wayne. Will Arnett’s gravel-voiced Dark Knight is hilarious, but beneath the relentless meta-humor and non-stop pop-culture references, the film hits real emotional notes about grief and Bruce’s self-destructive fear of opening up to others.
The plot kicks off when Batman crushes the Joker’s ego by telling him he means nothing to him. Hurt and seeking validation, the Joker gets himself banished to the Phantom Zone, only to break out with an army of cinema’s worst villains—including Voldemort, Sauron, and King Kong. To save Gotham, Bruce is forced to drop his solitary "lone wolf" act, step up as a father figure to the newly adopted Dick Grayson (Robin), and learn to lean on Barbara Gordon and Alfred. While the chaotic pacing and relentless visual noise can feel a bit overwhelming in the second half, its sharp writing, incredible DC Easter eggs, and surprising heart make it a lighthearted, thoroughly entertaining watch that still respects the core of the character.
Rating 7/10
![](images/mszmnho4.jpg)

title: Dr. STONE
content:
Dr. STONE delivered the absolute series packed with optimism, celebrating human ingenuity, curiosity, and the sheer joy of scientific discovery. The premise set a thrilling stage: 3,700 years after a mysterious green beam turned humanity to stone, high school genius Senku Ishigami awoke to rebuild human civilization from absolute scratch.
What made the entire journey so addicting was its grounded, step-by-step tech tree progression. Instead of hand-waving complex inventions, the show turned real chemistry, physics, and material science into a satisfying high-stakes puzzle. Watching Senku transform raw nature into chemical intermediates, industrial machinery, and eventually modern technology gave every small milestone a sense of hard-won victory. 
The cast and character dynamics elevated the narrative at every turn. Senku proved to be a uniquely refreshing protagonist, completely unbothered by traditional anime tropes or romantic distractions, remaining 100% focused on his passion for scientific progress and reviving humanity. The supporting cast rounded out his genius perfectly, with Chrome bringing raw intuition, Gen offering brilliant mentalist strategies, Ryusui driving global ambitions, and rival minds like Xeno raising the stakes. Even the central mystery behind Why-Man and the Medusa devices paid off with complete logical consistency, grounding even its sci-fi elements in firm physical rules.
Ultimately, Dr. STONE maintained its high-energy momentum all the way through to a deeply satisfying conclusion. It transformed what could have been a simple educational concept into a grand, epic adventure filled with brilliant strategic maneuvers and genuine heart. It stands as a masterclass in pacing and clever problem-solving, proving that a story built on human connection and intellectual curiosity can be just as thrilling as any action-heavy epic.
Rating - 9/10
![](images/mszitsoj.jpg)

title: Vinland Saga
content:
Vinland Saga was a frustratingly slow burn. 23 episodes of deliberate political setup for a few minutes of final payoff. The premise initially felt simple, and Thorfinn was frustratingly dumb—a kid so consumed by rage and misplaced pride that he spent his entire youth acting as a gloried slave for Askeladd, the very man who murdered his father.
Yet, as the story unfolded, Askeladd was revealed to be a masterclass in pragmatism and psychology, exposing the "warrior's code" for what it really was—a lie crafted by the strong to manipulate the weak. He used Thorfinn like a tool by dangling a "fair duel" in front of him for a decade. The ultimate irony, however, was his fate. The smartest man in the room, who mocked everyone for throwing their lives away for pride, ended up sacrificing his own life for Wales. He outsmarted the world, but karma caught up, and he died trapped in the very system he despised.
What made this series stick with me wasn't the action, but the brutal reality check it offered on human nature. It threw absolute idealism (Thors) against cold realism (Askeladd) and corrupted pride (Thorfinn), proving that in a world driven by greed, envy, and scarcity, no single philosophy guarantees safety. We aren't the ocean; we’re just drops in it, and fate eventually crushes everyone. In the end, Thorfinn was left empty, robbed of his revenge, showing that hatred only yields a hamster wheel of misery.
Ultimately, Vinland Saga isn't just a Viking story—it's a metaphor for the human condition. "Vinland" represents that hypothetical happy future we all hold onto in our heads just to keep moving forward in a bitter world. While the pacing tested my patience as a thriller fan, it forced me to look in the mirror and wrestle with hard truths about life, revenge, and what it truly costs to survive.
Rating: 9/10
![](images/mss8jwhd.jpg)

title: Pluto
content:
Rating - 9.5/10
A beautifully written story with a powerful emotional core. On the surface, it's a detective mystery, but at its heart, it's a story about human emotions—love, hatred, grief, hope, and the question of whether robots can truly feel them.
The series made me realise that humans can be the real monsters. If a robot is given every human emotion, it can become a monster too. But the story doesn't end there—it reminds us that not all humans are monsters, and that's what makes Pluto ultimately a story about hope.
Making Gesicht the protagonist was the best decision. Experiencing the story through a detective's perspective transformed it into a gripping psychological thriller instead of a conventional superhero narrative.
The pacing is slow in the beginning, and there were moments where I felt like skipping ahead for a few seconds. I'm glad I didn't. The final three episodes deliver an incredible payoff, tying everything together in a satisfying and emotionally impactful way.
The animation is modern and gorgeous, though I couldn't help but notice that almost every character seemed to have the same nose! I often had to rely on hairstyles and clothing to tell them apart.
Overall, Pluto is a tightly written, emotionally rich story that rewards patience. Every major character feels important, every emotion carries weight, and the ending leaves a lasting impact. I absolutely loved watching it.
![](images/ms6e19zk.jpg)

title: My Home Hero
content:
Rating – 9/10
A brilliantly written crime thriller with an extremely satisfying ending. The last two episodes were absolutely nail-biting, and the payoff was worth every minute.
The biggest strength of the series is Tetsuo. He's not a detective, a fighter, or a genius with unlimited resources—just an ordinary father who uses his intelligence, composure, and whatever is available to protect his family. I love intelligent characters who stay several steps ahead, and Tetsuo is one of the best examples of that.
His wife, Kasen, deserves just as much credit. She wasn't merely supporting him; she became his true partner in crime and in life. Their trust in each other made the story even more compelling. I also liked that their daughter remained unaware of the nightmare unfolding around her, which meant Tetsuo truly succeeded in protecting his family.
Kyoichi never felt like a typical villain. He was simply trying to uncover what he believed was the truth. The same goes for Matori—he was doing what he thought was right from his perspective. But the difference is that both of them were part of a mafia organisation. Their sense of "right" was built on a morally corrupt world, so eventually karma was bound to catch up with them.
The animation may not be exceptional, but the writing more than makes up for it. Every conversation, every decision, and almost every scene contributes to the bigger picture. There are very few wasted moments, making it a tightly written psychological crime thriller from start to finish.
![](images/ms4rme6c.jpg)

title: 91 Days
content:
Rating – 9/10
Excellent writing and a fully revenge-driven slow-burn drama. Although the story makes it clear from the beginning where it's heading, the plot is so tightly written that it kept me engaged until the very end. You know it's a revenge story and have a rough idea of the outcome, yet the way events unfold and the killings happen is unpredictable—you can never be sure what will happen next.
What I loved most is that it isn't just about revenge. It's equally about friendship, trust, acceptance, loyalty, and the motives that drive people. The characters are morally grey, making every decision feel meaningful.
Overall, it's a gripping one-night binge with excellent storytelling and a satisfying, thought-provoking ending.
![](images/ms4117i5.jpg)

title: Odd Taxi
content:
Rating - 9.5/10
Odd Taxi is a masterpiece of storytelling. It keeps the audience hooked through pure mystery, with almost every clue hidden inside seemingly ordinary conversations. Every character has a purpose, every dialogue has meaning, and every payoff feels earned, making the story incredibly satisfying from start to finish.
Odokawa was my favourite character—a kind-hearted, intelligent man whose calm and observant nature carried the entire series, while the diverse cast each with their own motivations and flaws, added remarkable depth to the story. The series also explores themes of obsession, loneliness, and the consequences of seemingly small decisions.
One of the strongest aspects of Odd Taxi is its attention to detail. The story rewards observant viewers with subtle hints and clever foreshadowing that make every revelation feel natural rather than forced. Even after predicting a few twists, I was impressed by how carefully everything was planned and connected.
My only criticism is that I would have preferred a stronger sense of closure in the ending. Other than that, Odd Taxi is a masterclass in mystery writing and one of the finest examples of tightly written storytelling in anime.
![](images/ms32r24t.jpg)

title: The Batman 2022
content:
Review 9.5/10
It's been a long time since a movie impressed me this much through pure visual storytelling. The Batman isn't just another superhero film; it's a gripping detective thriller where every frame has a purpose. The cinematography is phenomenal—the tracking shots, first-person camera angles, rain-soaked Gotham, rooftop silhouettes, and the dark red-orange colour palette make every scene unforgettable.
I never thought Robert Pattinson would become such a convincing Batman. He completely shed the "Twilight" image and delivered a brilliant performance. Even while wearing the cowl, he conveys so much emotion through his eyes alone. One subtle detail I loved was Bruce wearing sunglasses inside Wayne Manor. It perfectly shows how Batman has consumed his life—he's spent so much time in darkness that even daylight feels uncomfortable.
The Batsuit is another highlight. It isn't just stylish; it feels practical and realistic, built like a tank to absorb bullets and heavy impacts. I also loved that the film finally showed the black eye makeup instead of making it magically disappear like previous Batman movies. Small details like these make the world feel grounded and believable.
Overall, The Batman is a masterclass in cinematography and visual storytelling. It trusts the audience, lets the visuals speak louder than dialogue, and delivers one of the most immersive and realistic interpretations of Batman I've ever seen.
![](images/ms1so7cv.jpg)

title: Lord of the Rings
content:
I finally understand why The Lord of the Rings is regarded as one of the greatest trilogies ever made.

For years I avoided it, thinking it would be too long and slow, but I couldn't have been more wrong. It isn't just a trilogy—it's an epic. A timeless legend that feels like a story you'd tell your grandchildren.

Every character has a purpose and grows throughout the journey. Samwise Gamgee completely stole the show for me. His loyalty, courage, and friendship made him the heart of the trilogy. Aragorn's transformation into the true king was inspiring, while Gollum was one of the most unique and tragic characters, showing how completely the Ring could corrupt someone.

The world-building is breathtaking. From the peaceful Shire to Moria, Rivendell, Helm's Deep, and Mordor, every place felt alive and unforgettable. The battles were spectacular, but what stayed with me most were the characters and their relationships.

This trilogy deserves all the praise it has received over the years. It's not just a fantasy adventure—it's a masterpiece of storytelling, friendship, sacrifice, hope, and courage.

Rating: 10/10.
![](images/ms1ses3i.jpg)

title: Made In India, The Titan Story.
content:
Rating - 7/10
After spending weeks watching intense crime thrillers, dark dramas, and morally complex stories, The Titan Story was a refreshing change of pace. It wasn't trying to shock me with twists or keep me on the edge of my seat every minute. Instead, it told a simple, heartfelt, and inspiring story about how one of India's most iconic brands grew from a small idea into a household name.
One thing I really appreciated was the use of real photographs and archival footage throughout the series. It blurred the line between drama and documentary, making the events feel authentic and reminding me that this wasn't just fiction—it was the story of real people, real struggles, and real achievements.
The biggest reason this series resonated with me is because I personally own a Titan watch. The series is heartwarming because there is no unnecessary chaos, no over-the-top villains, and no forced drama. It's simply about vision, perseverance, innovation, and the people who believed they could build something extraordinary. Sometimes that's exactly the kind of story you need after consuming darker, more emotionally demanding content.
It may not be a masterpiece filled with suspense or unforgettable twists, but it doesn't need to be. It succeeds by making you appreciate the journey behind a brand that millions of people know today. By the end, I found myself looking at my own Titan watch with a new sense of respect.
If you're looking for a calm, inspiring, and elegant series that celebrates ambition, craftsmanship, and Indian entrepreneurship, The Titan Story is definitely worth watching.
![](images/ms1sc40d.jpg)

title: Se7en
content:
To be honest, this was my first time watching such a strange and unsettling crime mystery thriller. It wasn't just about solving a serial killer case—it was a psychological battle that kept me completely hooked from beginning to end. Every crime scene raised more questions than answers, and I genuinely couldn't take my eyes off the screen.

The atmosphere was dark, tense, and depressing in the best possible way. The constant rain, the grim setting, and the slow unraveling of the mystery created an unforgettable experience. The performances by Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman complemented each other perfectly, with one driven by emotion and the other by wisdom and experience.

The ending, however, left a bitter taste. It wasn't the kind of ending that gives you satisfaction or relief—it leaves you disturbed and thinking long after the credits roll. I genuinely felt bad for Detective Mills. No matter what decision he made in those final moments, John Doe had already trapped him in a situation where there was no real victory. That is what made the ending so heartbreaking.

One aspect I found fascinating was the concept of the Seven Deadly Sins. Before watching this film, I had only heard the term but never knew its history or meaning. The way each murder symbolized one of the sins—Gluttony, Greed, Sloth, Lust, Pride, Envy, and finally Wrath—was both creative and horrifying. It transformed the movie from a simple serial killer investigation into a philosophical story about morality, human flaws, and obsession.

Overall, Se7en(seven) was unlike anything I had watched before. It constantly kept me engaged, rewarded careful attention, and delivered one of the most memorable endings in thriller history. It's not an easy film to watch because of its disturbing themes, but it's definitely one that stays with you long after it's over.

Rating: 9.9/10
![](images/ms1rxlvt.jpg)

title: The Sheep Detectives
content:
I loved this movie and would give it a solid 9/10.

I suspected the killer about halfway through, but that's probably because mysteries like this are right up my alley. The plot wasn't particularly difficult to crack, yet it never stopped being engaging. The humour landed perfectly, and the sheep completely stole the show. Each one had a unique personality and special trait, and I loved how those characteristics were used throughout the story, leading to genuinely satisfying payoffs by the end.

I'd been waiting for its OTT release ever since I saw the trailer, and I'm happy to say it lived up to my expectations. It's been a long time since I've watched a cozy, witty mystery that was this entertaining. Charming, funny, and thoroughly enjoyable from start to finish.
![](images/ms1rrisd.jpg)

title: Devil May Cry
content:
Review (9/10)
This was a very morally grey series. Right up until the finale, there were mysteries waiting to be solved, and even by the end, several questions remained unanswered, leaving plenty of room for the next season.
What stood out the most was that, despite the large-scale conflicts, the series often felt surprisingly grounded—almost like a slice-of-life story at times. Every major character had their own beliefs and convictions, and none of them felt entirely right or wrong. As those ideals clashed, they naturally spiralled into chaos, making the conflict feel believable rather than forced.
The character development was strong, and the emotional moments landed well, adding weight to the action and the overarching story. Overall, it was an engaging series that balanced mystery, emotion, and stylish action effectively.
![](images/ms1gviuj.jpg)

title: Attack on Titan
content:
"If you win, you live. If you lose, you die. If you don't fight, you can't win. Fight. Fight!"
— Eren Yeager
Attack on Titan is not a story about good versus evil. It is a terrifying, masterfully written autopsy of human nature, inherited hatred, and the devastating cost of freedom.
The tragedy of Paradis was an engineered genocide. King Karl Fritz’s "peace" was an act of supreme cowardice and self-delusion. He erased his people's memories, trapped them in a cage to suffer for the sins of ancestors they knew nothing about, and waited for the world to wipe them out while he lived in comfort.
And what of the outside world? They were no noble victims. They sought revenge for atrocities their ancestors suffered—atrocities they never actually experienced themselves. Instead of breaking the cycle, they weaponized history, brainwashing younger generations with manufactured hatred and dangling false promises of equality—all while using Eldians as nothing more than livestock for their wars, while global leaders cheered for the total extermination of Paradis. They didn't see human beings; they saw monsters. They wrote their own death warrant when Willy Tybur declared total war to roaring applause.
Eren Yeager didn't start the war—he finished it. Faced with an absolute binary choice between the extermination of his friends or the destruction of the world, Eren chose to break out of the cage. The Rumbling was terrifying, horrific, and devastating... but it was the exact righteous vengeance 100 years of torment demanded. In a world that gave Paradis no choice, Eren answered with total, absolute power.
"Humanity will never stop fighting each other... until our numbers drop to one or less."
— Erwin Smith
From King Fritz’s insatiable greed, to Ymir’s 2,000-year tragic imprisonment, to Mikasa’s ultimate sacrifice that finally broke the Titan curse, Attack on Titan traps the viewer in an uncomfortable truth: hatred breeds hatred, and violence is an unending cycle. Eren gave his friends long, peaceful lives, but he couldn't rewrite human nature itself.
Attack on Titan isn't a comfortable show, and it doesn't give you clean morality. It forces you into a corner where you realize that when pushed to the absolute edge, monsters aren't born—they are created by the world around them.
Final Score: 10/10 — A cinematic masterpiece that will be talked about for generations.
![](images/ms15cdff.jpg)

title: Chainsaw Man
content:
Rating: 8/10
Chainsaw Man looks like a simple action anime about a boy who fights monsters, but underneath it is a strange and unpredictable story about loneliness, dreams, and human desires.
Denji is unlike typical anime protagonists. His simple goals and unusual personality make him both funny and surprisingly relatable.
The series stands out because it doesn't follow normal shonen rules. It is violent, weird, emotional, and unpredictable.
Denji is quite a character of its own. I love watching him do absurd things on screen. The amusement part of the series is it's strongest. Animation and Character design put on more stars.
It is very bloody and I liked the way it did not feel gross.
![](images/ms154823.jpg)

title: Jujutsu Kaisen
content:
Rating: 8.5/10
Jujutsu Kaisen brings a modern approach to the supernatural battle genre with stylish fights, unique abilities, and memorable characters.
The cursed energy system, intense battles, and unpredictable nature of the story make it highly entertaining. The series balances comedy with darker themes, creating a world where even powerful characters are not always safe.
The biggest strength is its characters, especially the chemistry between the main cast and the presence of Gojo.
The story is ongoing and I will love to watch it as it progresses.
![](images/ms14yre9.jpg)

title: Demon Slayer
content:
Rating: 9/10
Demon Slayer combines a simple but emotional story with some of the best animation in anime. Tanjiro's journey is not only about defeating demons and saving his sister, but also about holding onto his humanity in a cruel world.
The series shines through its characters, emotional battles, and unforgettable fight sequences. While the story may not be the most complex, the execution makes every major moment impactful.
Ufotable's animation takes the action to another level, making every fight feel cinematic.
I have also completed the Manga of demon Slayer and it was one of the best stories so far, not because it was very complex, but because the main character never gave up. Character designs are very beautiful and the story itself feels like a lore/epic.
![](images/ms14w5xr.jpg)

title: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
content:
Rating:9/10
The bond between Edward and Alphonse is the heart of the series. Their journey is not just about gaining power but about accepting their mistakes and finding a way to restore what they lost.
The world-building, character writing, and balance between action, comedy, and emotional moments make it one of the most respected anime of all time. Even in the early episodes, the series shows that every action has consequences.
The story follows a mystery which kept me gripped to the screen until the end. Emotional stakes are high. I would just say I loved the series. I can totally understand how it became one of the most famous and praised stories of its time.
![](images/ms14ojbn.jpg)

title: Solo Leveling
content:
Rating: 9/10
Solo Leveling delivers one of the most satisfying power progression stories in modern anime. Watching Sung Jinwoo evolve from the weakest hunter into an unstoppable force is the biggest attraction of the series.
While the story is simple compared to more complex anime, the hype moments, animation, and main character aura make it extremely entertaining.
I have also completed the Manga on the main story line, and it is a good read. People will disagree but I loved the show and would re-watch it just for animation quality and aura farming moments.
![](images/ms14he49.jpg)

title: The Misfit of Demon King Academy
content:
Rating: 8/10
The Misfit of Demon King Academy is pure entertainment from start to finish. Anos Voldigoad completely owns every scene with his overwhelming confidence and ridiculous power. The series doesn't try to hide how overpowered its protagonist is—instead, it embraces it, making every victory fun to watch.
I had mixed feelings about the show during the initial episodes, but as the story progresses I got a good hang of it. The ending was quite an unexpected but satisfying one. 
![](images/ms1467u8.jpg)

title: Overlord
content:
Rating: 8.5/10
Overlord stands out by telling the story from the perspective of the world's most powerful ruler instead of the hero. Ainz Ooal Gown is a fascinating protagonist whose intelligence and strategic thinking are just as impressive as his overwhelming strength. Combined with excellent world-building, memorable side characters, and political intrigue, Overlord delivers a unique take on the isekai genre because it does not follow the usual formula of a weak hero becoming powerful and saving the world.
Instead, it asks:
"What happens when the strongest being in the world is not the hero?"
The main character is morally grey, has very faithful subordinates, and can go extents for the welfare of him and his subordinates. Sometimes Ainz feel sorta dumb, but overall it feels amusing to watch him on screen.
![](images/ms140ggf.jpg)

title: Kuroko no Basket
content:
Review: 8/10
Kuroko no Basket takes the simple idea of basketball and turns it into an intense battle of talent, strategy, and determination. At first glance, it may look like a normal sports anime, but it quickly becomes a story about ambition, teamwork, rivalry, and the meaning of true strength.
The story follows Kuroko, a seemingly ordinary and unnoticed player who was once part of the legendary "Generation of Miracles"—a group of five extraordinary basketball players who dominated middle school basketball. Unlike his former teammates, Kuroko's strength is not raw power or skill, but his ability to support and bring out the best in others.
The arrival of Kagami, a talented and ambitious player with incredible physical abilities, creates the perfect contrast. Their partnership becomes the heart of the series: Kagami represents overwhelming individual talent, while Kuroko represents teamwork and strategy.
What I liked the most:
Every major opponent feels unique.
Matches are not just about scoring points; they are battles of mind games and different philosophies.
The Generation of Miracles are memorable because each one represents a different idea of basketball.
The rivalry between players keeps the story exciting.
Extremely hype matches.
Players with almost "superhuman" abilities (not realistic basketball).
Strong character development.
Tournament-style progression.
The story is about proving that basketball is a team sports and hardwork, passion, teamwork, can absolutely beat talent and arrogance. 
![](images/ms13root.jpg)

title: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Slums
content:
Rating: 8/10
The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Slums is a fun and relaxing fantasy anime with a likable overpowered protagonist. It balances comedy, action, and wholesome moments without taking itself too seriously. While the story is simple, the charming characters and satisfying main character moments make it an enjoyable binge.
![](images/ms13iizn.jpg)

title: Blue Lock
content:
Rating: 8/10
Blue Lock offers a unique take on sports anime by focusing on individual ambition over teamwork. The intense matches, creative strategies, and constant competition keep the series engaging throughout. While some games feel stretched out, Isagi's development and the evolving rivalries make it an entertaining watch. Overall, it's a refreshing football anime with exciting moments and a strong premise.
There is a significant downgrade in animation quality in season 2 but the story is tight enough to keep one engaged. Moreover everything feels worth watching for the last episode of season 2.
Eagerly waiting for S3.
![](images/ms13f874.jpg)

title: Parasyte
content:
Rating: 9/10
Parasyte: The Maxim is much more than an action anime—it is a story about humanity, identity, and survival. Shinichi's transformation from an ordinary teenager into someone emotionally conflicted and mentally stronger was one of the best aspects of the series. His character development felt natural and meaningful.
What stood out the most was Migi. Rather than being a typical companion, Migi represented pure logic, making every decision based on reason rather than emotion. The contrast between Shinichi's humanity and Migi's rational thinking made the story thought-provoking.
The action was intense, but the emotional and philosophical themes left a much stronger impact. It constantly made me question what truly defines a human and whether monsters are always the ones who look different.
![](images/ms13406r.jpg)
Overall, Parasyte delivers an engaging story with memorable characters, meaningful themes, and excellent pacing, making it a highly enjoyable watch.

title: Akame Ga Kill
content:
Rating: 8.5/10
Akame ga Kill! stayed true to its premise from start to finish. Despite the title, the story is really Tatsumi's journey. He was never the strongest character, but his growth from an emotional, reckless boy into a capable warrior was well written and believable.
Every member of Night Raid had a unique role, making every loss emotionally impactful. What I appreciated most was the moral complexity—while some characters fighting for the Empire were truly evil, others had genuine beliefs and reasons for their actions.
With only 24 episodes and little to no filler, the series delivers a complete story about a rebellion against a corrupt government, backed by exciting action, memorable characters, and great power systems. Overall, it was an engaging and highly enjoyable watch.
![](images/ms12uwm7.jpg)
